topIssues.title: op-acceptance-tests: TestProposerDefendsMultipleChallengedGamesConcurrently flakes on kona-sp1-proposer metrics port collision
topIssues.author: maurelian
topIssues.body:
`TestProposerDefendsMultipleChallengedGamesConcurrently` flakes with the proposer dying on boot:

```
kona-sp1-proposer | Error: failed to start metrics server:
  failed to create HTTP listener: Address already in use (os error 98)

Error Trace:  op-devstack/sysgo/zk_proposer.go:249
              op-devstack/sysgo/multichain_proofs.go:115
              op-acceptance-tests/tests/proofs/zk/zk_dispute_game_test.go:218
Error:        kona-sp1-proposer exited before its startup line was emitted
Test:         TestProposerDefendsMultipleChallengedGamesConcurrently
```

Seen in `memory-all-opn-op-reth-prague` ([build 5436840](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/jobs/5436840)). It took down `ci-gate`, which lists that job as `terminal`, so it blocks merge on an unrelated PR (#22290).

## Cause

`op-acceptance-tests/tests/proofs/zk/zk_dispute_game_test.go:252` is the F15 anti-pattern from [docs/ai/flake-prevention.md](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/docs/ai/flake-prevention.md#f15--selecting-a-free-port-before-starting-the-service):

```go
func freeTCPPort(t devtest.T) uint16 {
	listener, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
	t.Require().NoError(err, "reserve an ephemeral port")
	defer listener.Close()   // port released here
	return uint16(listener.Addr().(*net.TCPAddr).Port)
}
```

The port is released as soon as it's read, then passed to `kona-sp1-proposer` via `METRICS_PORT`. The proposer doesn't bind it until after `NewSimpleInterop` has stood up L1, the supernode, batchers, proposers and challengers — a multi-second window in which the kernel can hand that same number to any other socket. The number is drawn from the ephemeral range that every other socket in the process also draws from, and `#22208` (`op-acceptance-tests: run ZK dispute game tests in parallel`) put many more sockets in flight concurrently, which is what turned a latent race into an observed flake.

## Fixing it

Per F15, the owner of the socket should bind port 0 and report its address, rather than having the test preselect one. Two constraints make this more than a one-liner:

- `METRICS_PORT=0` currently means *metrics disabled*, and `zk_proposer.go:205-212` deliberately pins it so an inherited `METRICS_PORT` (op-succinct deployments export that exact name) can't leak into devstack proposers. So "0 = ephemeral" isn't available; the mode needs a distinct signal, e.g. `MetricsListen { Disabled, Ephemeral, Fixed(u16) }`.
- `metrics_exporter_prometheus` 0.18 binds inside `new_http_listener` and never surfaces the bound `SocketAddr`, and `with_http_listener` takes a `SocketAddr` rather than a listener — so the exporter can't report an ephemeral port, and can't adopt a listener we opened. Resolving the port inside the proposer therefore still needs a probe-then-bind, but the window collapses from seconds across processes to microseconds within one, and can be wrapped in a retry loop.

Sketch:

- `rust/kona/sp1/crates/proposer/src/config.rs` — parse `METRICS_PORT` into a three-state mode.
- `rust/kona/sp1/crates/host/src/metrics.rs` — `init_metrics` returns the resolved `SocketAddr`, retrying on `AddrInUse` in ephemeral mode.
- `rust/kona/sp1/crates/proposer/src/bin/kona-sp1-proposer.rs` — log the resolved address in the existing `metrics_addr` field of the `kona-sp1-proposer started` line.
- `op-devstack/sysgo/zk_proposer.go` — the startup-line callback already parses that log entry; capture `metrics_addr` and expose it.
- `op-acceptance-tests/tests/proofs/zk/zk_dispute_game_test.go` — drop `freeTCPPort`, scrape the reported address.

A cheaper interim mitigation, if the cross-language change isn't wanted yet: keep the preselection but make it recoverable — on `Address already in use`, pick a fresh port and restart the proposer. That leaves the race in place but makes residual failure negligible.

`freeTCPPort` has one caller today, so the blast radius either way is small.

topIssues.title: Holocene-D: Pipeline improvements tracker
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Tracking (non-blocking) observations and todos from https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/12506

- [ ] Garbage collect left-over state in state multiplexers?
- [ ] Refactor `Reset` to be called recursively on previous stages? So going from a _horizontal_ model, where the pipeline iterates over the stages and `Reset`s each, to a _vertical_ model where each stage owns the previous and resets it. There's only a single Reset that actually makes a network call (`L1Retrieval.Reset`), while all other resets simply clear some fields and slices, so there's no real value in _stepping_ through each reset individually. Note that this is actually more consistent to how each stage also fetches data from the previous stage (`prev.NextData` etc) - it is not fetched by the pipeline on each stage and then passed on to the next stage. I also choose to make `FlushChannel` work with this vertical ownership model as well. (And the Rust implementation of the DP also works with the same model.)
- [ ] Clarify if the `DepositsOnlyPayloadAttributesRequest` case in `EngDeriver.onPayloadProcess` can actually happen. To the best of my understanding the FCU call should already fail before during derivation.

See also https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/12444

topIssues.title: op-node: clarify sequencer field names (post-#22241 rename pass)
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Mechanical rename pass over `op-node/rollup/sequencing/sequencer.go`. **Blocked on #22241 merging** — deliberately kept out of that PR so its reviewed diff stays readable.

Zero behaviour change. Every name below is an unexported package-local except the receiver, so `lsp rename` (or equivalent) covers all callsites; nothing outside `op-node/rollup/sequencing` moves.

### Actively misleading — the reason this issue exists

| Current | New | Why |
|---|---|---|
| [`latestHeadSet chan struct{}`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/74905c43489d0f50f9a3c9a734fa8096cbed765c/op-node/rollup/sequencing/sequencer.go#L129) | `headKnownCh` | Reads as a bool or a set of heads. It is a one-shot channel, closed when the head first becomes known, then nil'd. |
| [`latest BuildingState`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/74905c43489d0f50f9a3c9a734fa8096cbed765c/op-node/rollup/sequencing/sequencer.go#L122) | `building` | The only one of five `latest*` fields that is not a block ref, and the only one meaning "current job" rather than "latest known X". Matches the `BuildingState` type and the `Building()` accessor. |
| [`latestHead`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/74905c43489d0f50f9a3c9a734fa8096cbed765c/op-node/rollup/sequencing/sequencer.go#L124) | `unsafeHead` | It *is* the unsafe head (`setLatestHead(x.UnsafeL2Head)`), and it sits directly beside `latestSafe`. Asymmetric: one names its safety level, the other does not. Also aligns with engine vocabulary (`UnsafeL2Head`). |
| [`latestSafe`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/74905c43489d0f50f9a3c9a734fa8096cbed765c/op-node/rollup/sequencing/sequencer.go#L127) | `safeHead` | Other half of that pair. |
| receiver `d` (31 methods) | `s` | A fossil from when this code lived in the driver: `d.l1OriginSelector` reads as driver state. Largest line count (~324), lowest risk — uniform substitution inside one file. |

### Terse rather than wrong — worth it while the file is already churning

| Current | New | Why |
|---|---|---|
| [`l ctxlock.Lock`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/74905c43489d0f50f9a3c9a734fa8096cbed765c/op-node/rollup/sequencing/sequencer.go#L69) | `mu` | `l` collides visually with `log` and `l1*` and scans as a length. With `inboxMu` alongside it, `mu`/`inboxMu` reads as a deliberate pair. |
| [`nextActionOK bool`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/74905c43489d0f50f9a3c9a734fa8096cbed765c/op-node/rollup/sequencing/sequencer.go#L114) | `nextActionArmed` | "OK" says nothing; it means an action is scheduled. `RunLoop` already uses `armed` locally. |
| [`latestSealed`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/74905c43489d0f50f9a3c9a734fa8096cbed765c/op-node/rollup/sequencing/sequencer.go#L123) | `lastSealed` | Different *kind* from the ingested `*Head` fields: a block **we produced**, possibly not canonical. `last` for our own history, `latest` for observed state. |

### Explicitly out of scope, so it is not re-litigated

- `eng SequencerEngine` — `engine` would shadow the imported `engine` package. `eng` is correct.
- `stalledByMaxSafeLag`, `awaitingResetConfirm` — long, but each states exactly one condition.
- `attrBuilder`, `toBlockRef`, `spec`, `BuildingState.Started` — fine. `StartedAt` is a marginal gain on an exported field now read from `op-e2e`; not worth the blast radius.
- `inbox` / `drainInbox` / `handleIngest` — local and obvious in context.

### Verification

`git show --stat` should touch one package plus the two `Building()` uses in `op-e2e/actions/helpers/l2_sequencer.go`, with no test *logic* changes. Then:

```
go test -race ./op-node/rollup/sequencing/...
go test -p 2 ./op-e2e/actions/...
just lint-go
```

🤖 *Co-created with Claude (Opus 5)*

topPRs.title: docs: regenerate op-reth CLI reference at v2.4.1 via new gen-op-reth-cli pipeline (IA slice 9)
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Matthew Cruz** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1784834359611159?thread_ts=1784834359.611159&cid=C0BHEH8TG91)_

IA-modernization slice 9 (final slice of the lane) per [`projects/docs-improver/plans/iteration-2/ia-modernization.md`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/solutions/blob/main/projects/docs-improver/plans/iteration-2/ia-modernization.md): the op-reth CLI regeneration pipeline, plus its first regeneration at `op-reth/v2.4.1`.

## Before / After

**Before:** the 59-page op-reth CLI reference was a one-time snapshot of the retired Vocs site with no regeneration pipeline. It silently drifted from every op-reth release — missing whole command families (`proofs`, `db migrate-v2`, `p2p enode`), documenting seven `db settings set` subcommands the binary no longer has, and carrying stale flags and help text on 51 pages.

**After:** the reference is regenerated from the current finalized release (`op-reth/v2.4.1`) and gains a documented, review-gated regeneration pipeline for future releases. Readers get 21 new command pages (including the whole `proofs` family), 51 corrected pages, and the 7 retired pages redirect to the surviving `db settings set` page that documents the replacement `v2` flow. The hand-written CLI overview gains one table row (`proofs`).

## How

- **Pipeline** — new `docs/public-docs/scripts/gen-op-reth-cli/` (`main.mjs` + `README.md` + `manifest.json`): a zero-dependency Node port of upstream reth's `docs/cli/update.sh` + `docs/cli/help.rs` (the exact tooling whose output format the original snapshot matches). It walks a pinned release binary's `--help` tree and emits the MDX pages (`diataxis: reference` frontmatter), the docs.json nav fragment for the collapsed "op-reth CLI reference" group (hand-written `cli/overview` guarded as the group's first entry, never touched), and provenance in `manifest.json`. Environment-dependent help output (home paths, version/target triples, CPU-count defaults) is scrubbed with upstream's replacement set.
- **Provenance chain** — binary built from source at tag `op-reth/v2.4.1` (tag commit `a9a8dad3f15`, the latest finalized non-rc release), which pins upstream reth at rev `f2eecc65482a`. `manifest.json` records `{tag, binaryVersion, sha256-over-generated-tree}`.
- **Idempotency** — running the generator twice against the same binary is a byte-for-byte no-op (verified live: second run reports `0 new, 0 changed, removed 0`, `git status` clean). `--check` mode recomputes the whole tree in memory and fails on any divergence, so hand edits to generated pages cannot survive review.

## No CI wiring (per Matthew's ruling)

Nothing in this diff touches `.circleci/`, `.github/`, or any package script; nothing runs unattended. Regeneration is registered as a **review-gated Mintlify docs automation** (see the README's "Automation registration" section, mirroring the gen-flags precedent in `DOCS_CONTRIBUTING.md`): when a newer finalized `op-reth/v*` tag exists than the manifest's, a regeneration is *proposed for human review* — never merged by CI. All 79 changed files live under `docs/public-docs/`.

## Regeneration drift (first run at v2.4.1)

| Kind | Count | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New pages | 21 | `proofs` family (7 pages), `db copy`, `db migrate-v2`, `db state`, `db prune-checkpoints` (3), `db stage-checkpoints` (3), `db checksum rocksdb`, `db get rocksdb`, `db settings set v2`, `p2p enode` |
| Updated pages | 51 | Genuine drift: new flags (e.g. `--tx-channel-memory-limit`, `--rpc.disable-metrics`, `--rpc-cache.max-bals`), renames (`--enable-discv5-discovery` → `--disable-discv5-discovery`), help-text and `--chain` list changes |
| Deleted pages | 7 | The per-table `db settings set <table>` leaves, superseded upstream by `db settings set v2` |
| Nav entries | 409 → 423 | +21 / −7; all other tabs and groups byte-identical, tab count 8 → 8 |

## Redirects (645 → 652)

| Change | Count | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New (R5, one per deleted page) | 7 | `/node-operators/op-reth/cli/op-reth/db/settings/set/<table>` → `.../db/settings/set` (the surviving parent documenting the `v2` flow) |
| Retargeted in place | 9 | The legacy `/rust/op-reth/cli/.../db/settings/set/<table>` entries (7 + 2 `*_in_static_files`) each pointed at a now-deleted URL; retargeted to `.../db/settings/set` so no chains or stale destinations exist |

Full 652-entry trace: 0 duplicate sources, 0 chains, 0 sources shadowing live pages, 0 destinations pointing at deleted URLs; no prose page links to any deleted URL.

## Deviations from the plan (stated plainly)

1. **7 redirects vs the plan's ~0–5 budget** — the estimate predates further months of upstream drift; every removal is the single superseded `db settings set` per-table family, all covered same-PR per R5 (plus the 9 in-place retargets the no-chain rule requires).
2. **Binary built from source (dev profile) instead of the release Docker image** — the release ships no binary assets and the image registry is egress-blocked in the build environment. Feature set matches the official image build (default features = DockerfileOp set); clap `--help` output is feature-dependent, not profile-dependent. Release metadata was injected exactly as the official image build does.
3. **One fork-specific scrub beyond upstream `help.rs`** — `default: op-reth/<VERSION>-<SHA>/<ARCH>`: the fork identifies as `op-reth/...` where upstream's scrub patterns only cover the `reth/...` spelling; without it the build-host arch would leak into a page. Recorded in `main.mjs` comments and the README.
4. **`manifest.json` carries `binaryVersion`** in addition to the gen-flags-precedent `{tag, sha256}` — extra provenance for a binary-derived generator.

## Verification (re-derived independently by the verifier)

- `--check` against the tag binary: exit 0 — 72 pages, nav fragment, and manifest all match the `--help` tree; manifest sha256 `e979848d9b4a…9017f6ad` re-derived independently and matches.
- `op-reth/v2.4.1` confirmed as the latest finalized (non-rc, non-draft) op-reth release via the GitHub API; `rust/Cargo.toml` at the tag pins reth rev `f2eecc65482a`.
- Sample pages (`proofs`, `db migrate-v2`, `p2p enode`, `node`, `db list`, `config`): flag sets match the binary's `--help` exactly; the 7 deleted commands are absent from the binary (`db settings set` now has only `v2`).
- Leakage sweep over all 72 pages: zero hits for the version string, commit SHAs, build timestamps, target triples, or build-host paths.
- Lints: `validate-nav.ts` OK (424 pages on disk / 423 nav entries / 1 allowlisted orphan — counts reconcile exactly), `validate-redirects.ts` OK (652 redirects, 11 grandfathered — baseline byte-identical to how IA-8 left it), `lint-link-policy.mjs` 0 findings. All 73 touched MDX files compile clean under @mdx-js/mdx.

## Wiz SAST findings (8 LOW) — addressed

Wiz flagged 8 LOW SAST findings on the PR head. The only SAST-scannable code in this diff is `scripts/gen-op-reth-cli/main.mjs` (everything else is MDX/JSON/Markdown), and its sinks account for exactly the two pattern classes Wiz LOW-flags in JavaScript: two `child_process` executions (`execFileSync` for `--help`/`--version`) and six dynamic-path `fs` operations (page write/mkdir/delete, docs.json write, manifest read/write, existing-page reads).

Context: this is a repo-local, review-gated generator that only shells out to a binary the operator explicitly passes via `--bin` (built locally from a release tag); it already used `execFileSync` with argument arrays (no shell), and every dynamic path is rooted at script-relative constants. The one genuine untrusted-input flow — subcommand names parsed from the binary's `--help` output feed both process arguments and file paths — is now hardened in `06bcbc29c9`: names are validated against the shape clap actually produces (`/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$/`, run aborts on anything else), and every page write/delete asserts containment inside the generated tree. No behavior change: `--check` still passes byte-identically at v2.4.1. The remaining dynamic-path reads/writes against script-relative constants (docs.json, manifest.json) are inherent to any generator and not reachable from untrusted input.

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Preview: the collapsed "op-reth CLI reference" group under Node Operators → Reference renders with `overview` first and nested subgroups in `--help` order (eyeball `db settings set` → `set`, `v2`)
- [ ] Spot-check a new page (e.g. `/node-operators/op-reth/cli/op-reth/proofs`) against `op-reth proofs --help` at v2.4.1
- [ ] Hit a deleted URL (e.g. `.../db/settings/set/receipts`) and confirm the redirect lands on `.../db/settings/set`
- [ ] Confirm the README's automation-registration section matches the intended Mintlify registry entry (review-gated, never CI)
- [ ] Agree the 4 deviations above are acceptable

## Program status

This closes the IA-modernization lane: slices 1–9 have all shipped. D12 is the program's last remaining content slice.

---

topPRs.title: op-alloy: make execution payload envelopes complete
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
## Overview

This draft repackages #22280, #22251, #22282, and #22284 into four review-focused commits while simplifying the execution-payload model and the gossip trust boundary.

`OpExecutionPayloadEnvelope` is now the structurally complete internal representation directly. Its V3/V4 variants require a parent beacon block root, while V1/V2 cannot carry one. This avoids introducing a second, isomorphic `OpNormalizedExecutionData` type.

The existing external formats are preserved:

- `admin_postUnsafePayload` and `conductor_commitUnsafePayload` retain the same JSON object shape through custom serde.
- CL P2P payload hashes and Snappy/SSZ encodings remain pinned to existing golden vectors.
- Engine API input remains represented by `OpExecutionData`, which can retain malformed sidecars until its fallible conversion into an envelope.

## Commit structure

1. **`op-alloy: make execution payload envelopes complete`**
   - Changes `OpExecutionPayloadEnvelope` into a V1–V4 enum with required V3/V4 roots.
   - Moves complete block and flashblock reconstruction directly onto the envelope.
   - Adds raw-byte block-hash checking that computes the transaction trie root without decoding transactions.
   - Converts fallibly from Engine API `OpExecutionData`, rejecting mismatched or noncanonical OP sidecars.
   - Converts infallibly back to canonical Engine API data.
   - Migrates Kona and op-reth directly to the complete envelope.

2. **`kona-gossip: authenticate payload bytes before decoding`**
   - Moves the signed P2P wire representation and Snappy codec out of Engine RPC types into a private `kona-gossip` module.
   - Represents the decompressed frame as a typed `Signature` plus exact encoded envelope bytes; the topic-derived version remains external.
   - Hashes and authenticates the exact received bytes before SSZ and transaction decoding.
   - Checks the claimed block hash from raw transaction bytes, matching op-node while leaving transaction validity to the EL.
   - Returns `OpExecutionPayloadEnvelope` from `BlockHandler`, `GossipDriver`, and the complete inbound call stack.
   - Preserves V1–V4 P2P bytes through moved golden-vector tests.

3. **`kona-engine: reuse inserted block info`**
   - Returns the `L2BlockInfo` already constructed by `InsertTask` and reuses it in `SealTask`.
   - Removes duplicate transaction decoding and block-info construction.

4. **`kona-node: validate admin unsafe payload block hashes`**
   - Performs synchronous raw-byte block-hash validation at `admin_postUnsafePayload` without decoding transactions.
   - Returns `InvalidParams` for malformed payloads or hash mismatches.
   - Enables the Kona invalid-CL-P2P-payload acceptance scenario.

## Benefits

- **Eliminates silent root defaulting.** Missing V3/V4 roots can no longer become `B256::ZERO`.
- **Makes structural invariants type-level.** V1/V2 cannot carry a root; V3/V4 always carry one.
- **Uses one complete payload abstraction.** There is no separate normalized type duplicating the envelope's variants and accessors.
- **Authenticates before expensive decoding.** Gossip signatures are checked against exact wire envelope bytes before SSZ decoding. Block hashes are then checked without decoding transactions.
- **Keeps transport details private.** Snappy framing, signature splitting, and topic-version decoding no longer leak through Engine RPC types or past the gossip validation boundary.
- **Validates Engine API boundaries.** Nonempty blob hashes, nonempty execution requests, and mismatched sidecar versions are rejected.
- **Prevents incomplete block reconstruction.** Complete conversion is available only on the complete envelope.
- **Produces canonical outbound sidecars.** Empty OP values and the fixed `EMPTY_REQUESTS_HASH` are synthesized correctly.
- **Preserves execution diversity.** Kona and op-reth continue to perform independent policy, execution, and state validation.

Authoritative execution validation remains in the EL. The synchronous CL check exists to provide immediate admin RPC feedback before asynchronous insertion.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p op-alloy-rpc-types-engine --all-features`
- `cargo test -p kona-engine -p kona-gossip -p kona-rpc -p kona-node-service --all-features -- --skip test_chain_label_metrics`
- `cargo test -p reth-optimism-payload-builder -p reth-optimism-flashblocks --all-features`
- `cargo check -p op-alloy-rpc-types-engine --no-default-features`
- `cargo check -p kona-engine --no-default-features`
- `cargo check -p kona-node --all-features`
- `cargo clippy -p op-alloy-rpc-types-engine -p kona-protocol -p kona-engine -p kona-gossip -p kona-rpc -p kona-node-service -p reth-optimism-evm -p reth-optimism-payload-builder -p reth-optimism-flashblocks -p reth-optimism-node --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc -p op-alloy-rpc-types-engine -p kona-gossip --all-features --no-deps`
- `cargo build -p op-reth --bin op-reth`
- `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND=kona-node DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-reth go test -parallel=1 -count=1 -run '^TestInvalidPayloadThroughCLP2P$' ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/sync/elsync/gap_elp2p/`

topPRs.author: wwared

## Claim

Replace four sequential Fault bond enrichers with one normalized bond snapshot and a sealed bond lane without changing existing Fault RPC order, metrics, logs, or boundary behavior.

## Base and dependency

PR 2 of 5. Base: `feat/zk-monitor-typed-lanes`; depends on #22225. Production ZK routing remains disabled.

Stack order: #22225 → #22226 → #22227 → #22228 → #22229.

## Commits and reading order

1. `55db68803d` adds the normalized snapshot and consolidated enricher while leaving them unwired.
2. `aae3cabe9c` atomically cuts extraction and every bond consumer over to the normalized snapshot.
3. `60eff34e4a` gives honest-actor bond metrics a single writer.

## Review focus

- Commit 1's recorded RPC trace and pinned block are directly comparable with the parent enrichers.
- Commit 2 preserves two deliberately different views: RPC recipients and expected-credit recipients.
- Fault nil tolerance, zero-address configuration, credit maturity, collateral, withdrawal, and forfeiture behavior remain unchanged. This PR adds no ZK behavior.

## Intentional behavior changes

None.

## Tests

- `mise exec -- go test ./op-dispute-mon/... -count=1`
- `mise exec -- just lint-go`
